original_query: SELECT t5.JOB FROM (SELECT JOB FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY JOB) AS t5 FULL JOIN (SELECT NAME FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME) AS t6 ON t5.JOB = t6.NAME GROUP BY t5.JOB
rewritten_query:
SELECT JOB
FROM EMP
WHERE ENAME = 'A'
GROUP BY JOB

UNION

SELECT NULL
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM DEPT d
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM EMP e
        WHERE e.ENAME = 'A'
          AND e.JOB = d.NAME
    )
)

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The FULL JOIN against the fully aggregated DEPT names is unnecessary. Since the outer query only projects t5.JOB and groups by t5.JOB, the original FULL JOIN + GROUP BY mainly adds a single NULL row when there exists an unmatched DEPT name. This can be rewritten using UNION with an EXISTS / NOT EXISTS anti-join condition.

The final GROUP BY t5.JOB is largely redundant because t5 is already grouped by JOB. It is only needed to collapse NULL rows coming from unmatched DEPT rows. Using UNION instead preserves correct distinct output while removing redundant aggregation.
Replace the FULL JOIN with an anti-join style EXISTS check so the database does not need to aggregate and join all DEPT names. This allows early exit once an unmatched DEPT name is found.
